article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Washington stunned Cincinnati on Monday night, the board still shows Week 11, and Thanksgiving week starts Wednesday night in Los Angeles.

items.headline: Washington stuns Cincinnati 22-20 on a walk-off field goal
paragraphs: Washington beat Cincinnati 22-20 on Monday night. Rookie kicker Drew Stevens kicked five field goals, including a 26-yarder as time expired, to win it.

Jayden Daniels drove Washington 64 yards in 34 seconds on the final drive. He hit rookie Antonio Williams on two long throws to set up the kick. Cincinnati led most of the night, but Washington scored on six straight drives to pull off the upset.
The app had Cincinnati by about 5 points and gave the Bengals about a 74 percent chance to win outright. The dog won outright. That is the whole lesson of the night, and it is in the next section.
items.takeaway: Washington 22, Cincinnati 20. Daniels drove 64 yards in 34 seconds, Stevens kicked the walk-off 26-yarder, and the underdog won outright.

items.headline: Thanksgiving week injury picture: Parsons nearing a debut, Ferguson out, several starters uncertain
paragraphs: Green Bay's Micah Parsons has been medically cleared after ACL surgery and is set to make his season debut Wednesday against the Rams, after limited practices Sunday and Monday. One other listing still shows him out, so treat his status as unresolved until the inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.

Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs, finger, was limited in Monday's practice and is listed questionable for Wednesday. Rams running back Kyren Williams was upgraded to full participation Monday. Rams defensive end Myles Garrett did not practice Monday with a knee issue.

For Thursday: Philadelphia cornerback Quinyon Mitchell did not practice Monday with a hamstring injury and his status is uncertain. Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith was a full participant, and running back Saquon Barkley was limited with a neck issue and an illness. Dallas tight end Jake Ferguson did not practice Monday and is out for Thursday with knee and ankle injuries.

Detroit tight end Sam LaPorta was limited Monday with an ankle injury. Chicago cornerback Kyler Gordon and running back Roschon Johnson both did not practice Monday, shoulder and ankle. Kansas City running back Kenneth Walker III did not practice with a groin injury, and tight end Noah Gray did not practice with a rib injury.
items.takeaway: Parsons is cleared and could debut Wednesday, but one listing still shows him out, so wait for inactives. Ferguson is out for Dallas on Thursday, and Mitchell, Barkley, LaPorta, Gordon, Johnson, Walker and Gray are all uncertain or limited.

items.headline: Rain and wind wait for Thursday night in Buffalo; the other games are indoors
paragraphs: Kansas City at Buffalo is the one outdoor game this week, Thursday at 8:20 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium. Rain is likely after 1:00 p.m. Thursday, with a high near 41 degrees, and rain is expected through the night. Wind runs about 9 to 13 mph from the east, gusting into the 20s.

The other two Thursday games are under cover. Chicago at Detroit kicks off at 1:00 p.m. ET at Ford Field, a dome. Philadelphia at Dallas kicks off at 4:30 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium, a retractable roof, with sunshine and a high near 55 expected outside.

Wednesday night is indoors too. Green Bay visits the Rams at 8:00 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium. So the only weather to watch this week is Buffalo on Thursday night, and the forecast can still move before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Thursday night in Buffalo: rain likely, near 40 degrees, wind gusting into the 20s. The Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Rams-Packers games are all indoors, so weather is not a factor there.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: No cards yet this morning - the board has not flipped to Week 12
paragraphs: The app still shows Week 11 this morning. The board was generated at 12:08 a.m. ET and is fresh, but all 13 Week 11 games lack a provider event, the market boards are empty, and all three headline cards read no play. There is no Week 12 line in the app yet, so there is no card to follow.

That is normal for a Tuesday morning after a Monday night game. The board refreshes every morning and evening, and the Week 12 lines land when it flips. Check the evening board for the first Week 12 cards.

When the board flips, the cards will be there the same way they always are. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. Balanced is the strong pick without paying too much. Value is the model's plus-expected-value play. If your book already has a Week 12 number you like, type the line and the price into Check and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator before you bet it.
items.takeaway: No Week 12 cards this morning because the board has not flipped yet - all three lanes read no play with empty market boards. Check the evening board for the first Week 12 lines.

items.headline: A 74 percent chance still loses about one time in four
paragraphs: Last night the app gave Cincinnati about a 74 percent chance to win outright, and Hit Rate was the Cincinnati moneyline. Washington won 22-20.

That is not the model being wrong. A 74 percent chance means the other side wins about one time in four, and last night was that one time. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
The point of the cards is to price the chance honestly, not to promise the result. When a favorite loses, the question is whether the price was fair for the chance, not whether the pick lost.
items.takeaway: Cincinnati at about 74 percent still lost. A probability is not a promise - the favorite wins about three times in four at that number, and last night was the fourth.

items.headline: Handle vs. tickets: two different crowds
paragraphs: Two numbers get quoted about where the betting is going, and they measure different things. Tickets, labeled BET, is the share of the number of bets. Handle, labeled HND, is the share of the money.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical example. Say 70 percent of the bets are on the favorite, but only 40 percent of the money is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite and fewer, bigger bets on the underdog. The crowd and the money are pointing different ways.

That split is interesting, not a pick. One book's split is only one book, and a split alone never tells you which side is right. What it tells you is to ask why the money disagrees with the crowd, and to watch whether the line moves toward the money before you bet.
items.takeaway: Tickets count the bets, handle counts the money. When they point different ways, ask why before you pick a side - and remember one book's split is only one book.

items.headline: Week 11 closed with the dog winning outright after the line moved the other way
paragraphs: The last real movement of Week 11 came before Monday night kickoff. FanDuel moved a full point toward Cincinnati, from -5.5 in the morning to -6.5 in the evening. DraftKings held -6 but the price moved from -113 to -120. Totals ticked down about a point.
Washington won 22-20 outright. The line moved toward the favorite all day, and the underdog won the game. Movement is information, not a result.

There is no new movement to report this morning because the app has no Week 12 lines yet. The board still shows Week 11. When it flips, this section picks up the Week 12 openers and tracks them against the results.
items.takeaway: FanDuel moved a full point toward Cincinnati before kickoff, DraftKings' price moved from -113 to -120, and Washington won 22-20 outright. No Week 12 lines in the app yet, so no new movement this morning.

items.headline: No games today - the week starts Wednesday night in Los Angeles
paragraphs: There is no football today. Week 12 starts Wednesday night, Green Bay at the Rams, 8:00 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium. Thursday brings three games: Chicago at Detroit at 1:00 p.m. ET, Philadelphia at Dallas at 4:30 p.m. ET, and Kansas City at Buffalo at 8:20 p.m. ET.
Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff, and that is when the last injury questions get answered. Parsons, Jacobs, Mitchell, Barkley and the rest stay open until then.

There is nothing to rush this morning. When the evening board flips to Week 12, look at the cards, and if your book has a number you like, run it through Check first. A good number today beats a hoped-for number later in the week, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
items.takeaway: No games today. Week 12 starts Wednesday night, Green Bay at the Rams, then three Thanksgiving games Thursday. Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff.

items.headline: Log the losers too
paragraphs: Settlement is manual here. Nobody settles your bets for you, so the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself.
Log the losers the same night you log the winners. A tracker that only holds wins is not a record, it is a highlight reel, and it cannot tell you what is actually working.
items.takeaway: Settlement is manual, so the tracker only works if you log the losers too. A record with only wins cannot tell you what is actually working.
